key: Behold, I have refined thee, but not as silver; I have tried thee in the furnace of affliction.
s: Midway through rebuking obstinate Jacob, spared for His name’s sake, the LORD recalls his trials; Radak, on 48:10, reads it as a refining short of the refiner’s, who removes the dross, since then few would have remained, the wicked afflicted but not wholly cut off.

evidence.gloss: But not as silver: not like a refiner of silver, for the refiner removes all the dross from the silver and consumes it until nothing but refined silver is left; I did not do so, for few would have remained had I done so; but the wicked among you, who are the dross, I afflicted with sicknesses, captivity, bereavement of children, or in the fruit of cattle or of the ground, as written in the curses, not to cut them off altogether.

reason: CORRECTED for the critic’s one problem, which holds: the context clause had no subject or verb. It now reads ‘Midway through rebuking obstinate Jacob, spared for His name’s sake, the LORD recalls his trials;’ (day.js: 48:4 obstinate, 48:8 treacherous, 48:9 anger deferred for My name’s sake). The clause was compressed and, as the critic allowed, ‘all’ dropped from ‘removes all the dross’ (the refiner’s removing the dross still carries כל הסיגים), so the sentence stays at 45 words. The reading is the reverified one, unchanged: re-opened packet.js tanakh 139 --verse 48.10, Radak on ולא בכסף, not like the silver refiner who removes all the dross, for few would have remained, but afflicted the wicked, the dross, not to cut them off מכל וכל.
